Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:
jbab...@vt.edu (Jason Babbitt) wrote:
> Well, I'm finally going to post my *maybe* unbeatable combat
>deck. I haven't constructed it, or played with it yet, so it's purely
>speculative. I would appreciate input. If you can think of a way to
>beat it, please tell me. Here it is....
> I've got mostly Hidden Lurkers/Earth Melds. Some Protean and
>Obfuscate cards. A fair number of Bum's Rushes. Maybe a couple of guns.
>I don't need old vampires, young ones with obfuscate or protean are best.
> I have to wait until I have two vampires. Then, I Bum's Rush my
>opponent. I strike first, Earth Meld, untap. My other vampire plays
>Hidden Lurker, my opponent has no strikes, I hit him (possibly with a
>gun), I press with the Hidden Lurker (perhaps I'll include some press
>cards as well). I Earth Meld, untap. My first vampire then plays Hidden
>Lurker and repeats what the last one did. This continues until my
>opponent is in torpor, leaving me with one vampire tapped and no damage
>at all. Note also that since I allways get first strike, my opponent
>cannot end combat. He can block the Lurker, but then I'll simply move my
>combat to whoever blocked. So, basically, one of his vampires goes to
>torpor, but he gets to choose which one. One possible escape is Elesium.
>Another is Mariel.
> Please tell me what you think.

Peace Jason,

Sounds very card intensive (more so than a regular combat deck). Wouldn't
work against another combat deck, Brujah Pot/Cel, for example, as the Brujah
could easily press to end combat or Immortal Grapple one of your vamps and
pound it into mush.

Nil carborundum illigitimi,

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
jbab...@vt.edu (Jason Babbitt) writes:

> I don't see how a combat deck could beat this deck. I will
>almost allways have an Earth Meld in my hand.

Well, combat decks beat up Combat Ends decks with Immortal Grapple (the #1
method), Fast Reactions, or Hidden Lurker. Weather Control and superior
Drawing out the Beast can help too. You are right in that it is very rare
for a combat deck to have enough of these, except sometime IG,

>The beauty of this deck is
>that when I bum's rush my opponent, he gets no strikes, the only possible

>defense he has are presses, and I think I'll add press cards to the deck.

Fortitude is a defense against this as you will burn cards doing damage
about as fast as he burns them preventing the damage. One could also
maneuver and Drawing out the Beast (but that's a weird one).

>I also only need one vampire to block with since he can continually
>untap. So I only *need* two young vampires.

Ah yes, those unlimited untaps are paying us a visit in another
incarnation --

I've seen another (apparently) abusive use of Earth Meld - an
Obfuscate/Protean Deck with stealth, Claws, Earth Meld, and Laptops. Very
few decks stand a reasonable chance against it - it Earth Melds from
rushers, blocks with Earth Meld, and either sneaks past interceptors or
claws them. At the same time there's too many bleeds for a reasonable
bounce to work. About the only normal deck with a good chance is Brujah
rush, and that only with Immortal Grapple, which is a rare and should thus
not be an essential defensive card.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: Biomech8
Messages.Body:
I recently made a intercept/put them in torpor/combat deck designed to be
used against high stealth decks or magesty decks (it would have never been
made if I hadn't read Jason's hidden lurker/earth meld deck, which showed
me the effectiveness of the Lurker. I chose to use Fast Reaction in the
deck instead of Hidden Lurker because it is used as after blocking (which
is what my minions are going to be spending most of their time doing.)
Fast Reaction is also a reaction card instead of an action card so it
cannot be blocked. You also don't waste any strike cards in combat when
your opponent plays dodges or combat ends. I do have a question on the
use of both the HL and FR.

I know that while playing action modifiers/reactions and participating in
combat the order of card play goes acting minion and then blocking minion.
But what about the playing of Hidden Lurker and Fast Reaction? At first
I thought the acting minion would go first, but Hidden Lurker is a new
action by a new minion. Fast Reaction is in reaction to the original
combat ending so I think that it would be played before any new actions
could have the chance to be played (but Hidden Lurker is an action in
response to the combat ending). Or is it who every throws their card down
first (which could result in an argument). Though this has never happened
to me personally, it's something I wonder about.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
nwbe...@news.amherst.edu (Neil Bernstein) writes:
>Biomech8 (biom...@aol.com) wrote:
>: I know that while playing action modifiers/reactions and participating in
>: combat the order of card play goes acting minion and then blocking minion.
>: But what about the playing of Hidden Lurker and Fast Reaction? At first
>: I thought the acting minion would go first, but Hidden Lurker is a new
>: action by a new minion. Fast Reaction is in reaction to the original
>: combat ending so I think that it would be played before any new actions
>: could have the chance to be played (but Hidden Lurker is an action in
>: response to the combat ending). Or is it who every throws their card down
>: first (which could result in an argument). Though this has never happened
>: to me personally, it's something I wonder about.

>This HAS happened to me, and I'd like to hear a ruling about it. Thanks.

If Hidden Lurker is played as printed (and as officially ruled) - as
an Action, then Fast Reaction take precedence - since it is payed at the
tail end of the action prior to the action started by Hidden Lurker.

If Hidden Lurker is played as intended (and as once officially errata'ed) - as
an Action Modifier, then Hidden Lurker has precedence since it would be
played by the acting Minion's Methuselah, and the order for "slap" situations
is: Acting Minion/Methuselah, Blocking Minion/Methuselah ((D) actions),
Prey then Predator (blocking undirected actions only), then clockwise around
the table starting with the Prey of the acting Minion/Methuselah.

--

curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:

> Many people (including yours truly) consider Earth Meld one of the

> academic exercise. Those people who believe Earth Meld is OK also may

> object to your posted deck; it very cleverly uses the endless untaps to

> allow more or less endless combat activities; it will be very hard for

> them to maintain their position now that your deck can be cited as an
> example of what can be done with Earth Meld.

A hearty round of applause for this post!

I suggest that all the "combat ends" cards (Earth Meld, Form of Mist
and Majesty) be amended so that they cost one blood to play. Majesty
would then allow vampires with superior Presence to untap at no extra
cost.

Consider this: Skin of Steel costs one blood and prevents all damage
from all strikes this round, if you have superior Fortitude. Earth
Meld prevents all damage from all strikes this round *and* in every
possible subsequent round of combat. Admittedly, it does use up your
strike, but the ability to untap more than compensates. I'd say it
should cost at least as much to play as Skin of Steel.

Come on, WotC, admit you made a mistake, and *fix it*.

- Keith

Messages.Author: Biomech8
Messages.Body:
Vampire A (who has greater fortitude) enters combat with vampire B.
The round is at close range.
Vampire A uses hand damage (1pt), and Vampire B (who has an innate hand
damage of 2) uses hand damage
(2pts.)
Vampire A prevents both damage inflicted by Vampire B. Vampire B loses
one blood.
No additional strikes are made.
During the press phase both players want to play Pulled Fangs.

Vampire A did not take any actual damage (it was prevented), and Vampire B
took one, so I would assume that Vampire A could play Pulled Fangs, while
B could not.

If Vampire B had two Wolf Companions (so another 2pts. of damage would be
inflicted on A) does the 2 points count toward the playability of Pulled
Fangs? (since Vampire B didn't inflict the damage, the Wolves did)

Pulled Fangs:
Used during the press step, and counts up damage successfully inflicted
during the round.

>If Vampire B had two Wolf Companions (so another 2pts. of damage would be
>inflicted on A) does the 2 points count toward the playability of Pulled
>Fangs? (since Vampire B didn't inflict the damage, the Wolves did)

From: aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie)
Newsgroups: rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad
Subject: Re: Pulled Fangs
Date: 4 Mar 1995 20:20:33 GMT
Message-ID: <3jai2h$m...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>

Pulled Fangs just cares about the range the round is at, not the nature
of the damage inflicted upon the vampire whose fangs are to be pulled.
So a shotgun will do just as well as a chainsaw. Note that damage from
retainers such as Wolf Companion won't count when comparing damage inflicted.
